title: Manual Fabric deployment parameter contract
description: Defines the inputs a customer (or operator) supplies after manually provisioning a Microsoft Fabric workspace + Lakehouse. The manual path is built and proven FIRST (Decision 3): if these parameters drive a working end-to-end run, the automated REST provisioning script becomes a convenience layer over a known-good path rather than a single point of failure. The preflight validator loads this schema and FAILS LOUDLY on any malformed or inconsistent value before any pipeline runs.

workspaceName.description: Display name of the manually-created Fabric workspace.

lakehouseName.description: Name of the managed Lakehouse created in the workspace. Letters, digits, underscore; must start with a letter (Fabric naming rule).

oneLakeEndpoint.description: ABFSS path to the Lakehouse in OneLake. Form: abfss://{workspace}@onelake.dfs.fabric.microsoft.com/{lakehouse}.Lakehouse. For Microsoft-internal (msit) tenants the host is msit-onelake.dfs.fabric.microsoft.com. The notebooks write managed Delta here (Decision 2). Must be the OneLake DFS endpoint, never a blob endpoint. SOVEREIGN CLOUDS: the default pattern covers the commercial and msit hosts only; if your cloud uses a different OneLake DFS host, widen this pattern to include it (copy the exact host from the Lakehouse > Properties ABFSS path).

sqlEndpoint.description: SQL analytics endpoint host for the Lakehouse. Power BI connects here first (Decision 4: SQL endpoint before DirectLake). Host only, no scheme or database suffix. For Microsoft-internal (msit) tenants the suffix is .msit-datawarehouse.fabric.microsoft.com. SOVEREIGN CLOUDS: the default pattern covers the commercial and msit suffixes only; if your cloud uses a different SQL endpoint suffix, widen this pattern to include it (copy the exact host from the Lakehouse SQL analytics endpoint Settings).

capacityId.description: Optional. Fabric capacity resource id backing the workspace. Recorded for traceability; not required for the manual path.

environment.description: Deployment environment label. Restricted to non-production while the manual path is being proven.

privateNetworking.description: Set to true if the source storage account (or Lakehouse) is behind a private endpoint or storage firewall. Microsoft Fabric ingests via impersonation (the caller's identity), NOT managed_identity=system as Azure Data Explorer does, so the storage 'trusted Microsoft services' firewall bypass does NOT apply to Fabric. Declaring true here makes the preflight FAIL LOUDLY at deploy time instead of hanging deep in a notebook run with no clear cause. See https://github.com/microsoft/finops-toolkit/issues/2061. Leave false (or omit) for a storage account reachable by the Fabric workspace identity.
